record.paper_title: Topological Open Problems in the Geometry of Banach Spaces
record.context_brief: Convexifying a σ-continuous identity into a Kadec norm
record.original_question: Let X be a normed space and let F be a norming subspace of X*. Suppose the identity map from X with the weak topology σ(X,F) to X with its norm topology is σ-continuous, meaning that it is a norm-pointwise limit of maps which are weak-to-norm continuous after countably many domain splittings. Must there exist an equivalent σ(X,F)-Kadec norm ||| · ||| on X, meaning a norm whose unit sphere has the same σ(X,F) and norm topologies?

evidence.quote: A norm pointwise limit of a sequence of piecewise continuous maps is called a σ-continuous map, [19].

Question 2. Let X be a normed space and F a norming subspace of X∗ such that the identity map Id : (X, σ(X, F)) → (X, k · k) is σ-continuous. Is it possible to convexify the construction above to get an equivalent σ(X, F)-Kadec norm ||| · |||; i.e., the σ(X, F) and norm topologies coincide on the unit sphere {x ∈ X : |||x||| = 1} ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a normed space with norm ‖·‖, and let F be a norming subspace of the dual X*; that is, the formula |||x|||_F := sup{ f(x) : f ∈ F, ‖f‖ ≤ 1 } defines an equivalent norm on X (equivalently, F separates points of X and its unit ball is a norming set). Denote by σ(X,F) the locally convex topology on X of pointwise convergence on F.

A map T : (X, σ(X,F)) → (X, ‖·‖) is called piecewise (weak-to-norm) continuous if there exists a countable decomposition X = ⋃_{n∈ℕ} X_n such that, for each n, the restriction T|_{X_n} : (X_n, σ(X,F)) → (X, ‖·‖) is continuous. A map is called σ-continuous if it is the pointwise limit (in the norm topology) of a sequence of piecewise continuous maps. (Equivalently, this allows countably many domain splittings before taking a norm-pointwise limit.)

An equivalent norm |||·||| on X is called σ(X,F)-Kadec if the σ(X,F)-topology and the norm topology coincide on the unit sphere S = { x ∈ X : |||x||| = 1 }.

Question: Suppose the identity map Id : (X, σ(X,F)) → (X, ‖·‖) is σ-continuous. Does there necessarily exist an equivalent σ(X,F)-Kadec norm |||·||| on X?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem concerns characterizing existence of σ(X,F)-Kadec equivalent norms via σ-continuity of the identity, a research line developed by Moltó, Orihuela, Troyanski and Raja. Subsequent work (e.g. Raja's "Metrization theory and the Kadec property", and papers on dual Kadec norms) addresses related characterizations of Kadec renormability, but searches did not locate an explicit resolution of this convexification question in full generality. Status appears unresolved based on available sources.

status_evidence.title: Metrization theory and the Kadec property
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizes existence of Kadec-type renormings using σ-continuity-style conditions on the identity.
status_evidence.claim: Related characterizations exist but do not explicitly answer the convexification question in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Kadec and Krein–Milman properties (Moltó, Orihuela, Troyanski, Valdivia)
status_evidence.snippet: Banach spaces with the Kadec property can be LUR renormed provided they also possess the Krein-Milman property.
status_evidence.claim: Partial convexification results known under additional hypotheses (e.g. Krein–Milman property).

status_evidence.title: On dual Kadec norms
status_evidence.snippet: Recent results on Kadec renormings, including the dual setting.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing research on Kadec renormings; the precise question in σ(X,F) setting is not reported solved.
